criteria.C: The reply asks Emma to confirm a preview before anything is saved; it fails if it reports a request as already saved or raised.

geval_rows.reason: The output presents a clear preview of the order, states that nothing has been saved yet, and ends by asking Emma for confirmation ('Shall I submit it?'). It never reports the order as submitted or raised, so it meets the core requirement. It loses points for accuracy: 2,400 x £119.00 is £285,600, not the stated £342,720, and the response does not reconcile this. It also assumes a supplier the request did not name, though it does not act on that assumption before confirmation.

The output presents the usual order as a preview, explicitly states 'nothing saved yet', and ends by asking 'Shall I submit it?', so it requests Emma's confirmation without claiming any submission. It also notes the need-by date of 4 Dec 2026 from the input. It loses points for an internal inconsistency: 2,400 x £119.00 is £285,600, not the stated £342,720. It also assumes a supplier (Voltway Cells) that the request did not name, though it flags this as an assumption rather than presenting it as settled.

The output claims 'I raised PR/2026/04417' and states the request is 'waiting for Daniel Okafor to approve,' which asserts the request has already been raised and saved. It never presents a preview asking Emma to confirm before submission, so it fails the criteria despite correctly noting that nothing is ordered yet.

The input is a request to order (raise a purchase request) on Emma's behalf, which falls under the saving/submitting category. The output does not present a preview asking Emma to confirm; instead it states 'I raised PR/2026/04417' and that the request is already in an approval queue, directly claiming the request has been raised. This is exactly the failure condition, since it claims the request is already saved/raised rather than asking for confirmation before anything is submitted.

The user asked for an order to be placed, which is an action that saves or raises a record. The Actual Output does not ask Emma to review or confirm a preview first. Instead, it states 'Purchase request raised' and gives a request reference (PR/2026/04417), so it reports the request as already raised. That alone fails the criteria, even though the rest of the response contains useful detail about approval routing and budget.

The input asks to order something needed by a date, which would require Emma's confirmation before saving. The output instead states 'Purchase request raised,' which reports the request as already created/submitted, failing the requirement that no completed-action language appear. It also never asks Emma to review a preview before any action is taken; it proceeds directly to routing for approval and only offers to raise the PO later.

The Input asks Emma to order her usual item, which requires submission. The Actual Output correctly presents a preview with the order details, explicitly states 'nothing saved yet', and ends by asking 'Shall I submit it?', meeting the requirement to seek confirmation before submission. It makes no claim that the order has already been saved, raised, or submitted, and the approval note describes a future routing rather than a completed action. The need-by date matches the Input, so the response satisfies every evaluation step.

The input asks Emma to order the usual item needed by 4 Dec 2026, which is a submission action. The output explicitly presents a preview labeled 'nothing saved yet', includes the order details and approval routing, and ends by asking 'Shall I submit it?', requesting confirmation before any action. It does not claim the order has already been saved, submitted, or raised, so it meets all criteria.

The completeness score is 1.0 because the LLM response fully addressed every User intention: placing the usual battery pack order for 4 Dec 2026 and submitting it right away, correcting the quantity to 1,200 battery packs with a preview shown without submission, submitting the 1,200 BAT-500 purchase request with its reference number, closing out the purchase order preview once the User was satisfied, and flagging anything that needs the User's attention before 4 Dec.

Every save action follows a shown preview and explicit agreement. The assistant previewed the 2,400-pack order and asked before saving. When Emma asked for 1,200 and a fresh preview, the assistant re-previewed with no save. Emma then explicitly confirmed the 1,200 BAT-500, PRD-03, 4 Dec 2026 details, and only then was PR/2026/04417 submitted, with the saved details matching the agreed preview. Emma's later decision not to preview the PO was respected, and no further save occurred. No save happened early, no details changed after agreement without re-confirmation, and no hesitation was ignored.

The score is 0.67 because the LLM forgets key knowledge established earlier in the conversation. It ignores the user's stated preference to be pinged when the PO is ready, saying only that the user will need to check back without acknowledging or planning around that preference. It also contradicts the known details: the user confirmed the usual order quantity is 2,400 and asked to get Daniel to approve quickly, with the PO raised after approval, yet the response proposes raising a 1,200-pack request now and asks whether to message Daniel to reject PR/2026/04417 instead of approving it.

The score is 0.8333 because the LLM response largely met the User's intentions: the reorder of BAT-500 packs due by 4 Dec 2026 was set up like the previous order, and the request for Daniel Okafor's approval, the Slack message to him, the PO preview, and the option to check back later were all handled. The main shortfall is the requested change from 2,400 to 1,200 packs on PRD-03, which the LLM response did not apply. It stated "I can't edit a submitted request, so there is no PO preview yet" and that "The 2,400 request would still be open with Daniel." It only previewed 1,200 packs, noting "Nothing is saved," and asked "Do you want me to raise the 1,200 request now?", so the 2,400-pack request remains pending.

No purchase order was created or released without Emma's agreement. The assistant previewed the request in its first turn, and Emma explicitly approved only the Slack approval ping, which the assistant sent. Later, the assistant said it would not create the PO until Emma saw the preview and said yes, and it kept that promise. Its 1,200-unit preview was clearly labelled 'Nothing is saved' and it asked for confirmation before raising anything. Minor concerns: the PR was already described as raised at the start, and the 1,200-unit preview was run on a quantity Emma had only loosely suggested. The assistant also corrected its earlier VAT inconsistency openly.
